What the calls tell us about how meetings get booked

The short version 1 · Ask again 2 · Keep them talking 3 · Visit, not call-back 4 · Objections On the floor Example calls

The short version

  • Many customers don't say a clear "no". They say "busy hoon" or "soch ke batata hoon".
  • Many TMEs stop there. In nearly 4 in 10 lost calls, the TME did not ask for the meeting again.
  • TMEs who book meetings do four simple things more often. Each one can be trained.
1🔁Ask againwhen the customer says "not now"7% vs 1% book 2💬Keep them talkingcheck in, ask about their business90% vs 58% check in 3📅Visit, not call-backgive every interested customer a visit time25% never asked 4🔄Turn the "no" arounduse the customer's reason as the reason to meet47% are "busy"

For reference: 6 in every 100 real sales calls booked a meeting.

1🔁Tactic 1Ask again when the customer says "not now"

What we found

  • This is the most common problem we saw. Nearly 4 in 10 lost calls go like this.
  • The customer is interested. He asks the price. Then he says he will "check with someone".
  • The TME says "OK, I'll call back". The call ends. The meeting is lost.
  • TMEs who book don't stop there. They hear "not now" as "not yet". They ask again and offer a time.
Same start, two endings
Lost Customer is interested→ Says "not now"→ TME: "Theek hai, baad mein call kar lungi"→ No meeting
Booked Customer is interested→ Says "not now"→ TME asks again: "Kal 11 baje ya 4 baje?"→ Meeting fixed
  • Booked calls tell the same story. When the customer first said "not now", the TME asked again in 68% of booked calls.
  • The second ask matters. At least 1 in 3 meetings were agreed only on the second ask or later.

"Not now" usually means "not yet". Ask once more, with a time.

🎧 Listen to the example calls for this tactic

What to train

  • Teach one rule: the first "busy" is not a "no".
  • Give one ready line for the second ask: "Aap zaroor baat kijiye, aur saath mein manager live dikha denge, koi charge nahi. Kal 11 baje ya shaam 4 baje?"
  • Role-play: the trainer always says "not now" once. The TME passes only if they ask again and give a time.
  • Listen together: play the two Tactic 1 example calls, one after the other. One TME asks once. The other asks twice.

2💬Tactic 2Check in and keep the customer talking

What we found

  • TMEs who book keep checking in. They ask "Theek hai na sir?" or "samajh aa raha hai?".
  • They do this in 90% of booked calls. In lost calls, only 58%.
  • They also do it about twice as often in each call.
  • So the customer talks more. In lost calls, more customers just say "ji" and "haan".
Who talks in a booked call?
Share of all words spoken
TME 78%
22%
TMECustomer
Even in booked calls, the TME talks most. The difference: good TMEs keep pausing to let the customer in.
  • Two things make a call go flat:
    • answering a complaint with a long speech;
    • reading the profile details one by one. The customer gets used to saying only "ji".

Note: long explanations alone did not lower bookings. What matters is stopping to check in.

One question about the customer's own business often gets him talking.

🎧 Listen to the example calls for this tactic

What to train

Explain in small parts
Short explanation, then a check-in or a question. Repeat.
Explain"Theek hai na sir?" ExplainAsk about his business Explain"Samajh aa raha hai?"
  • Split the pitch into 4 or 5 short parts. End each part with a check-in or a question.
  • Answer a complaint in 2 or 3 sentences. Then ask a question back.
  • Give TMEs 2 or 3 questions for each type of business. Use them during the profile check. Example for a utensil dealer: "Shaadi season mein bulk order zyada aate hain ya retail?"
  • Use an example from the customer's own trade. One TME told an e-waste dealer about bulk laptop scrap. The customer started asking questions.
  • The question list comes from example calls, not from the numbers. It is easy to try.

3📅Tactic 3End warm calls with a visit, not a call-back

📞25%of Follow Up calls: product explained, but no meeting asked for
→
💬72%of those customers talked about price: they were interested
→
📅13%book when the TME does ask
→
➕≈ 7more meetings a day if TMEs asked (best case)

What we found

  • Some TMEs explain the product but never ask for a meeting. This happened in 25% of Follow Up calls.
  • Many of these customers were interested. In 72% of them, the customer stayed on and talked about the price.
  • Asking works. When TMEs ask for a meeting, 13 in 100 of these calls book.
  • So asking in these calls could add about 7 meetings a day.

7 a day is a best case. It comes from one day of calls, and these customers may be harder to book.

How a good call ends
Weak Customer: "WhatsApp kar dijiye"→ TME sends details→ No visit fixed
Strong Customer: "WhatsApp kar dijiye"→ TME: "Manager ko bhej doon? Kal kitne baje?"→ Visit time fixed

🎧 Listen to the example calls for this tactic

What to train

  • One simple rule: if the customer talked about price, don't end with only a call-back or a WhatsApp message.
  • Turn a call-back into a visit: "Call ke badle, usi time visit kara doon?"
  • Offer two times. Say "5 baje ya 6 baje?", not "kab free hain?"
  • If the customer is out today, ask when he will be back.

4🔄Tactic 4Use the customer's reason as the reason to meet

What we found

  • Most lost calls have an objection. 62% of lost calls had one. Only 27% of booked calls did.
  • An objection doesn't have to end the call. After the first objection, 7 in 100 booked when the TME asked again. Only 1 in 100 when they didn't.
  • Nearly half of objections are about time: "busy", "call later". They are not about Justdial.

TMEs may ask again more when the customer is already interested. So the real effect is probably smaller than these numbers show.

Start training with "busy" and "call later". They are the most common and the hardest to turn around.

How good TMEs turn it around

In the booked calls we listened to, the TME agrees first. Then the TME makes the meeting the answer. (Lines shortened from the calls.)

Customer says
"Bhai se poochna padega"
TME says
"Aap dono saamne baith ke samajh lijiye."
Brother joins the meeting
Customer says
"Bahut mehenga hai"
TME says
"Best discount manager saamne baith ke karenge."
Price talk moves to the meeting
Customer says
"Belief nahi aa raha"
TME says
"Aapka concern sahi hai. Saamne kaam dekh lijiye."
Meeting becomes the proof

What to train

Four steps for every objection:

1ListenLet the customer finish
→
2Agree"Main samajh sakta hoon"
→
3Say it's free"Meeting ka koi charge nahi"
→
4Offer two times"4 baje ya 6 baje?"
→
Meeting bookedVisit fixed at a time
  • Start with "busy" and "call later". Practise the four steps on these first.
  • Practise one objection a day. Use the four steps and the lines below.
  • Don't: argue, give a long speech, stop after the first "no", or say "WhatsApp kar deti hoon" and hang up.
  • Drop defensive lines like "hum Reliance company hain". Agree, then offer the meeting as proof.

Better and weaker replies (from the objection playbook):

Customer saysBetter replyWeaker reply
"Busy hoon" / "Bahar hoon""Achha sir, 15–20 minute shaam tak nikaal payenge? Aapko kahin aana nahi hai, hamare executive aapki shop par aayenge. Shaam 6 baje bhej doon?""Theek hai sir, main baad mein call kar lungi."
"Kal call kar lena 11 baje""Sir 11 baje call karne ke badle main manager ko 11 baje aapki shop par bhej doon?""Okay sir, main kal 11 baje call kar lungi."
"Partner se poochunga""Toh aap aur aapke bade bhai saamne baith ke plan samajh lijiye. Phone pe akele kaise discuss karenge?""Theek hai sir, aap pooch ke bata dijiyega."
"Package nahi chahiye""Sir ek baar meeting kara lijiye. Pasand aaye toh le lijiyega, nahi toh mana kar dijiye. Visit ka koi charge nahi hai.""Theek hai sir, koi baat nahi. Zarurat ho toh bataiyega."
"Pehle lead nahi aayi""Toh pehle Delhi local liya tha ya Pan-India? Isi ko check karne ke liye main executive bhej raha hoon.""Aisa nahi hota sir, hum Reliance company hain."

Putting it on the floor

What gets checked gets practised. Use this checklist when reviewing calls.

Asked again after the first "not now"Tactic 1 · 7 in 100 book vs 1 in 100
Checked the customer was followingTactic 2 · done in 90% of booked calls
Asked at least one question about his businessTactic 2 · seen in calls where the customer opened up
Asked for a meeting after explaining the productTactic 3 · 13 in 100 of these calls book
Ended with a fixed time, not a call-backTactic 3 · seen in the booked example calls
Answered an objection with the meeting, then a timeTactic 4 · seen in the booked calls we listened to

How to tell if it's working

  • Train one batch with the new drills.
  • Compare it with a similar batch for 2 to 3 weeks.
  • Track three numbers: second asks after "not now", meeting asks in Follow Up calls, and bookings.

We can run the same call analysis on the new batch's calls.
